summary: A safe, warm and readable batch: no gore, lines are short, and many single jokes land well (bus pulling away as you reach the stop, escalator that never climbed a step itself, toy jet 'crashed in nine hundred and still has both wings', submarine still looking for the bottom of the plughole, crane lifting a swimming pool onto a hotel roof, the builder's wellie stuck in the new path, the police goat chase that the goat won). Move mechanics are mostly respected: drain, heal, buff, stun and poison names fit, kit moves are sensibly re-skinned for non-engines (horse pat whiff, brake dust stink, coal smoke), and most variant Ultimates are effect-neutral. The structural problems are three. (1) Legendaries are templated: 29 of 79 are 'has done X for N years / since great-grandad / three generations', often ending on 'still has its original...' or 'never once...', with no outrageous achievement or punchline (barge, flagpole, pole, pedestal, shield, manhole cover, lifeboat, rowboat, scissor lift, oxcart, thresher...). (2) Monster names are paired with the wrong rarity's lore in about 30 objects, often as clean swaps (bus, car wheel, pole, lifeboat, rowboat, tugboat, backhoe, biplane, ambulance, scooter, satellite). (3) Premises repeat: inside objects (car wheel runaway x3, tugboat towing x4, dinghy capsizing x3, segway balance, backhoe C=L, barge C=L, bulldozer R=L, turnstile R=E, quad bike U=E), and across objects (paver U = road roller U; ambulance C = fire truck C = ferry C; ambulance R/E = fire truck E; horse cart E = oxcart E; dinghy U = sailboat U; rv/mobile home/station wagon Legendaries; rickshaw L = tuk tuk L; police R = bollard R; helicopter U = w03 hummingbird U). Epics lean on 'every Y in town / whole town / led a convoy / with a hundred others' (57 of 79 match), and several Rares are helpful talents rather than troublesome powers. Hard flags: trademark or real-person echoes (crane 'Lifting Klaxon', skid steer 'Little Bob', bulldozer 'Big Bertha', 'Montgolfiera', lifeboat 'Grace', 'Mister Sprinkles', scooter 'Hot Wheel Spin'), a church wedding setting (horse cart), a political echo ('never left a child behind'), a child alone at sea in a storm (dinghy L), rescue words on attack Ultimates (fire truck, lifeboat), and a few effect-specific Ultimate names on varying Ultimates (grille 'Glare', rowboat 'Sunny'). Every high and medium item has a concrete replacement; names were checked for length and uniqueness against all curated content and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Templated Legendaries: 'has done X for N years / since great-grandad / three generations', usually ending on 'still has its original...' or 'never once...', with no outrageous achievement or punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Keep at most a handful batch-wide. Write a single concrete outrageous act with a punchline (bible: 'Picked up a house to find the remote. It was in the sofa'). Replacements for the weakest are in the issues list.

patterns.pattern: Monster names describe another rarity's lore (often a clean swap between Common and Uncommon, or a rotation of three). Name and lore sit together in the encyclopedia, so this reads as an error.
patterns.suggestion: Write names after the lore, line by line (tracker lesson). Exact re-pairings are given per object.

patterns.pattern: One premise carried over several rarities of the same object instead of five premises.
patterns.suggestion: Let one trait own at most two rarities; use other real traits of the object (parts, sounds, owners, jobs, where it lives). Per-object rewrites are in the issues list.

patterns.pattern: Near-copies between objects in this batch, and with w01-w04.
patterns.suggestion: Pairs: paver U = road roller U ('moves so slowly that ... walk beside it'); ambulance C = fire truck C = ferry C ('just as you fall asleep'); ambulance R/E = fire truck E (traffic parts); horse cart E = oxcart E (whole harvest in one trip); police R = w06 bollard R (runaway shopping trolley); dinghy U = sailboat U (flapping sail, names Sailflapper/Sailflap) and dinghy E = sailboat E (regatta); rv L ~ mobile home L ~ w06 station wagon L (every campsite/beach, original cushions/sand); rv R ~ mobile home R; rickshaw L = tuk tuk L; motorcycle R = tuk tuk R; cherry picker C = scissor lift C = w06 gondola lift C (stuck halfway); grille L = steamroller L = w06 classic car L = hearse L (polished every Sunday/morning for decades); skid steer C = excavator U (spins like dancing); harvester U = thresher U (chaff); ice cream van R ~ bus C; helicopter U ~ w03 hummingbird U. Rewrite one side of each pair (issues name which).

patterns.pattern: Epic shape: 'every Y in town / the whole town / led a convoy/parade / with a hundred others', often with no disruption or no punchline (a fact plus 'everyone waved').
patterns.suggestion: An Epic needs large-scale chaos with a concrete funny consequence. Vary the frame: a single place going wrong, a chain reaction, a misunderstanding.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name formulas: most Legendaries start with Grand/Old/Lady/Sir/Captain/Big/Commander/Little, and stems repeat (Bertha x2, Puff- x2 here and more in w06, Rosie, Reggie, Rusty, '-alot', 'Queen of the ...').
patterns.suggestion: Vary shapes: a pun-name alone, a name plus a deed, a title that is a joke in itself. Avoid reusing a personal name across objects.

Klaxon (trademark), Little Bob digger (Bob the Builder), Big Bertha (WWI gun), Montgolfiera (Montgolfier brothers), Grace at a lighthouse (Grace Darling), Nightingale (Florence Nightingale, low), Mister Sprinkles (ice-cream-van trade-name pattern), Hot Wheel Spin (Hot Wheels). Object labels Segway, Model T and Jeep are brand names in the inventory; the writing correctly avoids repeating them.

patterns.pattern: Commons built on the same everyday nuisance: a slow vehicle in the lane at walking pace, or noise early in the morning / just as you fall asleep.
patterns.suggestion: Keep the best one or two (tractor, garbage truck) and give the others a nuisance tied to their own parts.

patterns.pattern: Rares that are helpful skills or pleasant events rather than a troublesome power.
patterns.suggestion: Rare = a memorable power that causes trouble (seed artillery, replaying real life to watch people trip twice).

patterns.pattern: Move names that contradict the mechanics: rescue or heat words on attacks and buffs, and status-specific words on variant Ultimates.
patterns.suggestion: Rescue Rush/Run -> an attack image; Glare/Sunny on varying Ultimates -> effect-neutral; Heat Shield (defup) -> a brace; Bubble Bath Torpedo (poison) -> something smelly.

patterns.pattern: Animal-reaction punchlines used as a crutch: every cow/goat/deer/giraffe/seagull looks up, watches or follows.
patterns.suggestion: Fine occasionally; prefer a human reaction or a concrete consequence.

patterns.pattern: Hit-and-run (x3) names with four or five repeats ('Spin Spin Spin Spin', 'Bounce Bounce Bounce Bounce', 'Chug Chug Chug Chug').
patterns.suggestion: Three repeats match three hits; vary with a different last word ('Chug Chug Bump').

issues.issue: 'Seatkicker' describes kicking seats, but the Common lore is about leaving the gate early while passengers are in the café.
issues.suggestion: 'Gatedasher'

issues.issue: Names are paired with the wrong lines: 'Loop-de-Loop' sits on the two-sets-of-wings Uncommon, 'Cropduster' on the loop-the-loop Rare (no crop dusting anywhere).
issues.suggestion: 'Twinwing' for Uncommon; 'Loop-de-Loop' moves to Rare.

issues.issue: Blowing a scarecrow's hat off is a stunt, not a troublesome power.
issues.suggestion: Consider a bigger consequence, e.g. it blows the whole haystack into the farmer's kitchen.

issues.issue: Rare, Epic and Legendary all scale one trait (soaring high/far/long quietly); the Epic has no disruption and a non-reaction punchline (cows didn't look up).
issues.suggestion: 'Circled silently over the beach all afternoon, and every seagull thought it was a giant gull and followed it home.' Name: 'Gullherder Glide'.

issues.issue: Another 'stays up a long time' line; 'the eagles asked how' is soft, and eagles reappear in w06 gondola lift Rare.
issues.suggestion: 'Stayed up riding warm air for a whole week. When it finally landed, the pilot had grown a beard and the airfield had a new café.'

issues.issue: 'Hilltopper' does not describe the Rare (climbing a thermal above the clouds); 'Cloudbase Climb' on the Epic describes exactly that Rare.
issues.suggestion: 'Cloudbase Climber' for Rare; the Epic gets its own name once rewritten (see Epic).

issues.issue: A glider has no exhaust, and 'Breeze' reads fresh on a poison move.
issues.suggestion: 'Muck-Spread Updraft' keeps the cow field and makes the stink explicit.

issues.issue: 'Strafe' means firing guns from the air; a little martial for a toy in a kids' game.
issues.suggestion: 'Sofa Swoop'.

issues.issue: 'Pretend Smoke' cannot poison anything; the joke undercuts the effect.
issues.suggestion: 'Hot Plastic Whiff' or 'Melted Plastic Pong'.

issues.issue: Same premise as the Rare (delivering things to places with no roads/airport).
issues.suggestion: 'Landed on the hotel swimming pool to deliver a birthday cake. The guests kept swimming round its floats as if it were a lilo.'

issues.issue: Delivering post is a helpful talent, not a troublesome power.
issues.suggestion: Give it a nuisance, e.g. its floats scoop up half the lake and drop it on the jetty.

issues.issue: Same launch-and-land-somewhere premise as the Rare (bunk bed to laundry basket; garden to next door's pond).
issues.suggestion: 'Blasted off from the garden with one stamp on the air pump and landed on the school roof. The caretaker now keeps a ladder ready.'

issues.issue: 'according to its owner' is the hedged 'according to its own story' frame the tracker bans; no concrete achievement.
issues.suggestion: 'Pumped so hard it flew over three gardens and the school, then landed back in its own toy box. Its owner calls this a full orbit.'

issues.issue: Heat word on a non-burn (self defup) move, against the tracker lesson.
issues.suggestion: 'Nose Cone Brace'.

issues.issue: 'Flashblue' sits on the mirror-writing Uncommon; 'Corner Racer' sits on the Rare about parting traffic with blue lights. Neither name matches its line.
issues.suggestion: 'Mirrorwriter' for Uncommon; Rare 'Bluelight Parter'.

issues.issue: Same premise as its own Rare (traffic parting for the blue lights) and as fire_truck Epic ('traffic parted like a river').
issues.suggestion: 'Turned on its siren once at the seaside, and every gull on the beach copied it until sunset.' Name: 'Gullsiren Chorus'.

issues.issue: 'Nightingale' strongly evokes Florence Nightingale, a real person.
issues.suggestion: 'Bluebell Dash, Fastest to the Rescue'.

issues.issue: 'Basket Bumps' collides with the signature 'Basket Bump' on the same monster.
issues.suggestion: 'Sandbag Shower' (plural, fits ×3).

issues.issue: 'Montgolfiera' is built on the Montgolfier brothers' surname (real people).
issues.suggestion: 'Wanderwind, Queen of the Breeze'

issues.issue: No punchline; 'with nothing but X and Y' is a template shared with motorcycle L and sailboat L.
issues.suggestion: 'Floated so high over the mountains that it landed on a summit, and the climbers who had walked up for a week were not pleased.'

issues.issue: Sheep following it is cute but not a troublesome power.
issues.suggestion: Optional; no change required.

issues.issue: Near-copy of road roller Uncommon ('Moves so slowly that ... walk beside it').
issues.suggestion: 'Leaves a road so warm behind it that every cat in the street comes to lie on it at teatime.' Keeps the name 'Hotroad', which then fits.

issues.issue: 'Bertha' repeats bulldozer 'Big Bertha' (itself the nickname of a WWI siege gun).
issues.suggestion: 'Tarmacia, Layer of Highways'

issues.issue: 'Every pothole in town' is the generic 'every Y in town' Epic shape.
issues.suggestion: Optional; no change required.

issues.issue: Same premise as the Legendary (pushes a hill/mountain, it ends up somewhere else).
issues.suggestion: 'Pushed a skip, a shed and the foreman's lunch into the same pile before noticing anyone was shouting.' Name: 'Pileshover'.

issues.issue: 'Big Bertha' is the nickname of a famous WWI siege gun and duplicates the paver's 'Bertha'.
issues.suggestion: 'Shovemore, Mover of Mountains'

issues.issue: Weak punchline (workers find something else to do).
issues.suggestion: Optional; no change required.

issues.issue: 'Gravelsmoother' sits on the blade-in-the-middle Uncommon; it describes the Common.
issues.suggestion: 'Beltbuckle Blade'

issues.issue: 'Dirt Road Smoothing' is an activity, not a creature name.
issues.suggestion: 'Eggsaver'.

issues.suggestion: 'Rolled over a forgotten garden hose and sprayed the whole street like a giant fountain until teatime.' Name: 'Hosesquasher'.

issues.issue: Common and Uncommon are both 'spins on the spot'.

issues.issue: 'Little Bob ... Digger' evokes Bob the Builder (trademarked character); toy truck repeats 'Big Bob'.
issues.suggestion: 'Pocket Pip, Busiest Digger'

issues.issue: 'Building Site Spin' does not describe the Epic (moving a sand hill, volleyball club moves in).
issues.suggestion: 'Sandhill Shifter'

issues.issue: Sand-becomes-a-beach overlaps dump truck Rare.

issues.issue: Duplicates road roller's 'rolled the street flat' Epic; no punchline ('every bump disappeared').

issues.issue: 'Since great-grandad was a boy' generations formula plus 'polished every Sunday' (grille L, classic car L, hearse L).

issues.issue: 'Iron Drum' does not describe the whistle Rare.

issues.issue: No punchline ('still had fuel to spare').

issues.issue: 'For forty years' N-years formula; soft punchline.

issues.issue: Near-copy of oxcart Epic (the whole harvest in one trip).

issues.suggestion: 'Holemaker' for Common; 'Clawarm' for Uncommon.
